aria: Animated recap of the Bulls' 125 to 117 overtime home win over the Hawks: Matas Buzelis' corner 3-pointer with 23.5 seconds left in overtime that made it 123 to 117, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Norman Powell's 33 points with 9 in overtime, the top scorers, how the Bulls won, and the next game at Minnesota.
notes: Box score from the Bulls' 125–117 overtime home win over the Atlanta Hawks at the United Center on Nov 13, 2026 (an NBA Cup group game), from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via FOX Sports and ABC News), the Chicago Sun-Times, the Chicago Tribune and Hawks coverage on Yahoo Sports, Yardbarker, Bleacher Nation, SI and ClutchPoints. All 125 Chicago points and all 117 Atlanta points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 60–53 Chicago at the half, 84–83 after three, 110–110 after regulation, 15–7 in overtime. Team totals (field goals 45 of 91 to 47 of 107, threes 20 of 50 to 8 of 40, rebounds 51–48, assists 34–29) are from the box score. Chicago's 18-point first-half lead is from Bleacher Nation, SI, Yardbarker and the Sun-Times; Atlanta's only lead after the first quarter came in overtime (AP; Yahoo Sports). The AP story lists Jalen Johnson with 16 points; the box score and every other source have 27, which is used here. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Atlanta's 13–4 run in the fourth quarter tied it at 103, with CJ McCollum scoring five straight (Bleacher Nation; Yahoo Sports), and Jalen Johnson's running dunk tied it at 110 with 1:08 left (Yahoo Sports). Onyeka Okongwu's driving layup gave Atlanta a 112–110 lead in overtime; Powell answered with a three-point play and scored 9 of Chicago's 15 overtime points (AP; Yahoo Sports; the Sun-Times). Powell, back from a two-game absence with back spasms, had a season-high 33 (Yahoo Sports; ClutchPoints). Josh Giddey's 15 points, 14 assists and 10 rebounds were his first triple-double of the season (the Sun-Times). The win snapped an eight-game losing streak; Chicago's only other win was at Milwaukee on Oct 23 (AP). The Bulls made a season-best 20 threes (Chicago Tribune via Yahoo Sports). Rookie Caleb Wilson missed the game with a broken right hand (the Sun-Times). Chicago plays at Minnesota on Saturday, Nov 14 at 8:00 PM ET (the site's schedule; Yardbarker).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Matas Buzelis' corner 3-pointer with 23.5 seconds left in overtime that made it 123–117 (the Sun-Times and the Chicago Tribune give 23.5 seconds; the AP says 23; Bleacher Nation calls it a corner three; the Hawks story on Yahoo Sports gives the 123–117 score). The recaps don't describe the move further, so it is drawn as the template's plain catch-and-shoot pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Chicago Bulls or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Buzelis’ listed 6-foot-8 and 196 pounds (RealGM), in Chicago's home white with No. 14 (RealGM). No wingspan from a reliable measurement is reported, so his arms are drawn at a 1.0 ratio. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
